newsitem.title: FRANCE: Poll shows French parliamentary race narrowing.
newsitem.headline: Poll shows French parliamentary race narrowing.

text.p: France's parliamentary election race is narrowing, but the ruling centre-right coalition remains in the lead a week ahead of the first round of the May 25-June 1 vote, according to a new poll made public on Friday.

The CSA poll for the French daily Le Parisien showed the centre-right with a margin of 43 seats over the combined left in the National Assembly, compared to a margin of 80 seats in a similar poll a week earlier.
The poll showed the centre-right with 299 assembly seats to 256 seats for the combined left and no seats for the far-right National Front.
The week-earlier CSA survey had given the centre-right 317 seats to 237 seats for the combined left and 1 seat for the National Front.

Both polls looked only at the 555 seats representing constituencies in mainland France and did not cover another 22 seats in overseas departments and territories, most of which are currently held by government candidates.
The poll relied on interviews with 1,008 registered voters and was conducted on Thursday and Friday.
